title: Sirtuin activators as an anti-aging intervention for longevity
abstract: Abstract Keywords Introduction Sirtuins in aging Sirtuin activating compounds Conclusions Abbreviations Declarations Publisher’s note References Copyright statement. Sirt5 is a mitochondrial enzyme, involved in metabolism and stress response, regulated largely by two proteins PGC-1α and AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). Overexpression of PGC-1α elevates cellular Sirt5 levels*,* while activation of AMPK down-regulates Sirt5 levels, playing a role in mitochondrial energy metabolism [33)]. Sirt6 also represses LINE1 retrotransposons by mono-ADP ribosylating the nuclear corepressor protein KAP1; however, with the increase in age of the mice and DNA damage, Sirt6 levels decrease, and the silenced retroelements are activated [45)]. Fisetin and luteolin suppresses oxidative stress by activating sirtuins like Sirt1, Sirt3, and Sirt6 and reducing expression of FOXO3a [103)]. Activation of the Protein Deacetylase SIRT6 by Long-chain Fatty Acids and Widespread Deacylation by Mammalian Sirtuins.
